newsitem.title: USA: Muni yields fall up to 15 basis points over week.
newsitem.headline: Muni yields fall up to 15 basis points over week.

text.p: Municipal bond yields dropped as much as 15 basis points in the week ended Thursday, erasing increases from the week before, Delphis Hanover Corp said Friday.
Treasury market yields did not fall as much as munis over the week, with the 30-year bond dropping seven basis points to 7.08 percent at Thursday's close from 7.15 percent the week before.
The market reversed course again Friday morning, after softer-than-expected economic data prompted a strong rally.

Smaller-than-expected inflation in the Consumer Price Index and a slow retail sales report Friday morning pushed the long bond yield down to 6.96 percent by midday, and municipal gains were said to be strong as well.

But as of Thursday's close, thirty-year Aaa-rated municipal yields had falled 10 basis points, to 5.75 percent, Delphis said. Thirty-year Baa yields fell 15 basis points, erasing a 15 basis point gain the week before, to settle at 6.50 percent.
In the intermediate sector, ten-year Aaa-rated muni yields were down five basis points to five percent. Baa-rated 10-years fell 10, to 5.75 percent.
Average yields on one-year Aaa-rated municipal bonds were down five basis points to 3.80 percent and Baa-rated one-years fell the same amount to 4.60 percent.
The Aaa municipal yield curve flattened five basis points, moving to 195 basis points. The spread between one-year and 30-year Baa's flattened 10 to 190 basis points.
The credit spread between Aaa-rated and Baa-rated one-years was unchanged at 80 basis points, and the 30-year spread narrowed five to 75 basis points.
